summary: Backend-only verification of the CallDrip-style Lead Call Engine + marketing form -> Lead Source routing. Created /app/backend/tests/test_lead_call_engine_ladder.py (20 pytest cases, all passing) covering: workflow config round-trip + 4-attempt clamp + single website catch-all, /api/lead-sources/website-pages, POST /api/demo-requests -> demo_requests/conversations/messages/lead_call_jobs Mongo assertions + attribution, scheduler firing attempt 1 (real Twilio call placed to +15005550006 test number, status 'ringing'), simulated Twilio voice webhooks (answer -> Gather 'Press 1', wrong token -> 'no longer available', Digits=2 -> pass, Digits=1 -> whisper with name/source/company/industry/comments + <Dial callerId timeout=30>+15005550166</Dial>), claim persistence to job/conversation/contact, second presser + post-claim answer -> 'already claimed', status callback -> 204 + calls[].status completed, in-app claim stopping the ladder (claimed_via 'app'), single-attempt ladder exhaustion via scheduler, page-specific text_only route creating NO call job, and regressions (GET /{source_id} not shadowed by /website-pages, list by store_id, legacy demo with no matching source, ai_routing_matrix 28/28). All test data purged; Website source restored (website_default true, contact_mode text_and_call, ladder = tester only, original intake_text).

critical.issue: NO AUTHENTICATION. Verified with plain curl (no Authorization/X-User-ID): PUT returned 200 and rewrote the Referral source workflow. An anonymous caller can therefore set contact_mode=text_and_call, put ANY user_ids on the call ladder and flip website_default/website_pages, i.e. hijack all inbound website leads and trigger real Twilio outbound calls to arbitrary internal users. Add auth + org/store scoping to the lead_sources router.

minor.issue: Only {{field}} placeholders are replaced. A source saved with single-brace {first_name} is SMS'd verbatim to the customer ('Hi {first_name}, thanks for booking a demo!' was actually sent during testing). Support {field} too or validate/normalize on save.

Full-replace semantics with Pydantic defaults: any omitted field is silently reset (va_enabled defaults to True, notify_all_on_intake True, claim_timeout_minutes 5, contact_mode text_only). A partial save from any client can turn the AI VA on or wipe the ladder. Consider exclude_unset / PATCH semantics.

next_attempt_at = now + max(next_delay, RING_SECONDS+5) silently floors every configured per-attempt delay at 30s, so delay_seconds < 30 (UI allows 0) is not honored. Document or clamp in the UI/validator.

Does not set claim_source='app' on the conversation (claim-and-call does). mark_claimed() is called directly so the job is still stopped, but the scheduler safety net (process_lead_call_jobs only skips when claim_source=='app') can't catch this path if mark_claimed fails.

pages[] merges arbitrary strings previously stored in website_pages, so stale/typo page keys ('demoreqid_test', 'idempotent_test') show up in the picker list. Consider returning only WEBSITE_PAGES plus routed extras flagged as custom.
No Twilio request-signature validation (relies solely on the per-job token, which is reasonable) and /answer is exposed over GET as well. Low risk, worth noting.

action_items: CRITICAL: add authentication/authorization to the lead_sources router (workflow GET/PUT, claim, claim-and-call) - currently fully open and can be used to place real outbound calls to any user.
Support single-brace {first_name} in hydrate_intake_text (or reject/normalize on save) so unhydrated placeholders are never texted to customers.
Make workflow PUT non-destructive for omitted fields (va_enabled currently defaults back to True).
Decide/document the 30s floor on per-attempt delay_seconds.
Set claim_source='app' in POST /api/lead-sources/claim/{conversation_id} for consistency with the scheduler guard.
critical_code_review_comments: lead_sources workflow endpoints have zero auth - verified exploitable with curl; this is the highest-priority fix.

_app_url() resolves to PUBLIC_FACING_URL (https://app.imonsocial.com), so Twilio voice webhooks from a preview-created job always hit production; a real rep answering a preview-triggered call hears 'no longer available'. End-to-end phone flow can only be verified in prod (webhooks were simulated here).
routers/lead_intake.py is 1933 lines and demo_requests.py 850 - both exceed the 700-line guideline; _fire_intake_workflow should be extracted into a service module.

start_call_workflow prepends lead_doc.assigned_to as attempt 1 with delay 0; if a source uses round_robin/weighted assignment the assignee is dialed even if they are not on the configured ladder - intentional per design, but it means assignment strategy can pull real users onto a text_and_call ladder.
lead_call_webhooks.claim uses eng.datetime/eng.timezone (module attribute re-export) instead of importing datetime directly - cosmetic but fragile.
seed_data_creation: Temporary demo_requests/conversations/contacts/messages/inbound_leads/lead_call_jobs for ladder-qa*@invalid.imonsocial.test and phones +1500555016[6-9]/0170, plus one manually inserted 'qa-token' exhaustion job. All purged by the module fixture at the end of the run (verified 0 leftovers). Pre-existing contacts from iteration 291 (+15005550141/0142/0188) were left untouched. Website source restored to website_default=true, contact_mode=text_and_call, ladder = Activation Tester only, original intake_text; Referral restored to text_only/no pages/va_enabled false.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Re-run: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_lead_call_engine_ladder.py -v -s (no xdist; tests are order-dependent and share module STATE). It purges its own data before and after; export LADDER_QA_KEEP=1 to keep data for inspection. SAFETY: only user 6a978d68b8673c29063aa8b9 (+15005550006) may appear on a ladder and only 500-555-01xx customer phones may be used - Twilio is live and real calls are placed (attempt 1 showed status 'ringing' with a real CallSid). Twilio voice webhooks point at https://app.imonsocial.com (PUBLIC_FACING_URL) so the answer/claim/status flow must be simulated by curl against the preview host. hydrate_intake_text needs {{double braces}}.
rca_of_the_issue: No functional defect in the engine itself - every requested behavior matched spec. The two notable findings are (1) the lead_sources router lacks any auth dependency, so workflow/claim endpoints are anonymous-writable (confirmed by an unauthenticated curl PUT returning 200), and (2) the review request's expected intake text 'Hi Ladder, ...' from a single-brace {first_name} template does not hydrate because hydrate_intake_text only replaces {{field}}; the raw placeholder was actually SMS'd to the test number.
